children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures were mixed and feeder cattle ticked higher on Friday, as traders positioned ahead of the weekend and the US Department of Agriculture's cattle on feed report, released after the close of the trading session.
ended the day unchanged at 231.125 cents per pound.
finished up 1.200 cents at 348.125 cents per pound.
Lack of fresh news and pre-weekend positioning resulted in lackluster trade on Friday, said Karl Setzer, co-founder of Consus Ag Consulting.

But after the session ended, the USDA released its monthly cattle on feed report, showing cattle on feed for slaughter as of October 1 at 100% of last year's numbers and just below the estimate of a Reuters poll of analysts that put them at 100.3% of the previous year.
Meanwhile September placements in feedlots were reported at 88% of last year's numbers, beneath the trade estimate of 92.6% and the lowest for September since 1996.
Wholesale boxed beef prices fell at midday on Friday to  $365.79 per hundredweight (cwt) for choice cuts, down $3.68 from the previous day, while select cuts rose $2.29 to $352.69 per cwt.

Beef packer margins fell into the red at the end of the week. Packers lost an average of $4.10 per head, down from profits of $32.15 on Thursday, and $70.90 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.
On Friday, 96,000 cattle were slaughtered, down from 102,000 a week ago, according to the USDA.
December lean hog futures (LHZ26) ticked up, ending 0.025 cent higher at 65.575 cents per pound.
The USDA reported prices for pork carcasses fell $1.14 to $74.09 per cwt, while bellies dropped $2.41 to $82.18 per cwt.
On Friday, 462,000 hogs were slaughtered, according to the agency, down from 472,000 a week ago.
